questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

## Verification Strategy

**Local Testing:**
```bash
# Install Kyverno
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Dry-run validate manifests
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f manifest.yaml

# Test policy against sample manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest manifest.yaml
```

**CI Integration (GitHub Actions):**
```yaml
name: Manifest Validation
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate with Kyverno
        run: |
          kyverno apply cluster-policy.yaml \
            --manifest manifests/ \
            --policy-report \
            --fail-only-on-exists
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to integrate image provenance with runtime governance in a GPU-driven, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It spans CI pipelines, admission controls, and cross-system attestations—core skills for securing production ML platforms.

## Key Concepts
- **Image Provenance**: Using cosign and Rekor to cryptographically verify container image origins
- **SBOM Signing and Verification**: Ensuring software bills of materials are tamper-proof and traceable
- **Central Provenance Store**: A single source of truth for validated digest information
- **Admission Constraints**: Kyverno/OPA policies enforcing GPU type and quota at deploy time

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Sign, generate SBOM, and attest
name: Gate: image provenance
on: [push]
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.COSIGN_KEY }}

jobs:
  build-sign-attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Generate and sign SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json=sbom.json
          cosign attest --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            --type sbom \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Upload to Rekor (automatic with cosign attest)
        run: |
          echo "Rekor entry created automatically during attestation"
      - name: Store central provenance digest
        run: |
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
          echo "${{ github.sha }}:$DIGEST" >> provenance_store.txt
```

```yaml
# Kyverno admission policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-gate
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "ghcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/org/*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
          verifyDigest: true
          required: true
    - name: enforce-gpu-type
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      context:
        - name: namespace
          apiCall:
            urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces/{{ request.namespace }}
      preconditions:
        - key: "{{ request.namespace }}"
          operator: NotEquals
          value: "kube-system"
      validate:
        message: "GPU type must match namespace label"
        pattern:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - (resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu"): "?*"
    - name: enforce-gpu-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      validate:
        message: "GPU quota exceeded for namespace"
        deny: |
          {{ exists request.namespace.metadata.labels."gpu-quota" }}
```


## Verification Steps

**Local verification:**
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type sbom --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Check Rekor transparency log
rekor-cli get --uuid <rekor-uuid>
```

**CI verification:**
```bash
# In CI pipeline before deployment
cosign verify \
  --key pub.key \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/org/ML-platform/.github/workflows/ci.yml@refs/heads/main" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical policy-as-code skills and integration of admission controls into CI for a multi-cloud, large-scale platform.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA ConstraintTemplate
- securityContext runAsNonRoot and runAsUser
- privileged and capabilities.drop
- hostPath/hostIPC/hostPID prohibition
- CI validation with kubectl/dry-run and Gatekeeper

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (high-level sketch)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sprivilege
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sPrivilege
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8sprivilege
      violation["privilege violation"] {
        input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
      }
```
```yaml
# Failing manifest (hostPath & privileged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-service
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
            runAsNonRoot: false
            runAsUser: 0
            capabilities:
              drop: []
      volumes:
        - name: data
          hostPath:
            path: /tmp
            type: Directory
```
```yaml
# Passing manifest (non-root, restricted caps, no hostPath)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-service
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
            privileged: false
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
      volumes: []
```

- Confirm PRs fail on bad manifests and pass on good manifests.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic manifest validation, API version awareness, and simple, repeatable CI gating for multi-service apps.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes manifests, apiVersion, kind
- Labels discipline (app, version)
- Image digests and internal registries
- Lightweight CI gates (GitHub Actions) and script-based checks

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in $(git ls-files '*.yaml' '*.yml'); do
  api=$(yq e '.apiVersion' "$f")
  if [[ "$api" == "apps/v1beta1" || "$api" == "extensions/v1beta1" ]]; then
    echo "Deprecated apiVersion: $api in $f"; exit 1
  fi
  if ! yq e 'has(.metadata.labels.app) and has(.metadata.labels.version)' "$f" >/dev/null; then
    echo "Missing labels in $f"; exit 1
  fi
  if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].image' "$f" | grep -q '@sha256'; then
    echo "Image must use digest in $f"; exit 1
  fi
done
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This tests your ability to design supply chain security for a Kubernetes monorepo where multiple services share base images - a critical skill for CKS certification and real-world cluster security.

## Core Concepts

**Signing vs Attesting:**
- **Signing** (cosign sign): Cryptographically proves an image hasn't been tampered with since it was built and signed
- **Attesting** (cosign attest): Attaches signed metadata (SBOM, provenance) to an image that can be verified later

**SBOM (Software Bill of Materials):**
- Lists all components, packages, and dependencies in an image
- Generated with: `syft image -o spdx-json`
- Standard formats: SPDX, CycloneDX
- Critical for vulnerability scanning and compliance

**SLSA Provenance:**
- Tracks the entire build pipeline (SLSA Level 3+)
- Contains "materials" field that references base image digest
- Enables tracing derived images back to their bases
- Predicate type: `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`

**OCI Referrers:**
- Modern way to store attestations alongside images in OCI-compliant registries
- Replaces older annotation-based approaches
- Supported by Harbor, GHCR, ECR, ACR, GCR

**Policy Enforcement:**
- **Kyverno:** Native Kubernetes policy engine with verifyImages rule
- **OPA/Conftest:** General-purpose policy as code
- Run in CI/CD (before `helm upgrade`) AND optionally as admission controllers

**Key Security Properties:**
1. **Base image integrity:** Verify base images are signed and attested
2. **Derivation chain:** Service images must reference an attested base
3. **Immutable records:** Rekor transparency log ensures no retroactive changes
4. **Automated enforcement:** No deployment without verified images

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes the ability to architect a scalable, multi-tenant security model in Kubernetes, balancing native features with a single control plane for runtime enforcement. It assesses identity, policy, and observable security outcomes under real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Pod identity via service accounts and SPIFFE IDs
- Mutual TLS with Istio for east-west and north-south traffic
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for least privilege
- NetworkPolicy-based segmentation
- Pod Security Standards and image signing (cosign) in CI/CD
- Telemetry, audits, and validation plans

## Code Example
```yaml
# Istio: mTLS
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic manifest linting and security checks in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes manifests
- YAML parsing with yq
- GitHub Actions gating
- SecurityContext and imagePullPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-manifest-gate.yml
name: Manifest Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          set -e
          violations=0
          for f in $(git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -E '\\.ya?ml$' ); do
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].readinessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].livenessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsNonRoot' "$f" | grep -q true; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsUser' "$f" | grep -q '1000'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].imagePullPolicy' "$f" | grep -q 'Always'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
          done
          if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
```

```python
# detector.py
import sys, yaml
def has_hostpath(path):
  data = yaml.safe_load(open(path))
  vols = data.get('spec', {}).get('volumes', []) or []
  for v in vols:
    if 'hostPath' in v:
      return True
  return False
if __name__ == '__main__':
  ok = True
  for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    if has_hostpath(f):
      ok = False
      print('HOSTPATH found in', f)
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to enforce Kubernetes scheduling best practices through automated CI gates. It demonstrates understanding of pod distribution for high availability, GitOps workflows, and infrastructure-as-code validation.

## Key Concepts

- **Kubernetes topologySpreadConstraints**: Controls how pods are distributed across failure domains (zones, nodes, etc.)
- **Deployment replicas and scaling**: Understanding when and why to distribute workloads
- **YAML parsing in CI pipelines**: Using Python or Node.js to validate manifests
- **GitHub Actions workflow configuration**: Building automated gates for GitOps
- **Local validation and pre-commit hooks**: Catching issues before code reaches CI

## Code Example

```python
# gate-topology.py
import sys
import yaml
import glob

def check_deploymentConstraints(doc):
    if doc.get('kind') != 'Deployment':
        return True
    
    replicas = doc.get('spec', {}).get('replicas', 1)
    if replicas <= 2:
        return True
    
    topology = doc.get('spec', {}).get('template', {}).get('spec', {})
    if 'topologySpreadConstraints' not in topology:
        return False
    
    for constraint in topology['topologySpreadConstraints']:
        if constraint.get('topologyKey') != 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone':
            return False
        maxSkew = constraint.get('maxSkew', 1)
        if maxSkew > 1:
            return False
    
    return True

def main():
    failed = []
    for manifest in glob.glob('**/*.yaml', recursive=True):
        with open(manifest) as f:
            docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
            for doc in docs:
                if doc and not check_deploymentConstraints(doc):
                    failed.append(manifest)
    
    if failed:
        print(f"Failing manifests: {failed}")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    print("All Deployments pass topology constraints check")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## GitHub Actions Workflow

```yaml
name: Topology Constraints Gate
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  enforce-topology:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install pyyaml
      - name: Run topology gate
        run: python gate-topology.py
```

## Failing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:latest
```

## Passing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: web
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:latest
```

## How to Verify

**Local Verification:**
```bash
pip install pyyaml
python gate-topology.py
```

**CI Verification:**
The GitHub Actions workflow runs automatically on pull requests. Merges are blocked until all Deployments with replicas > 2 include proper topologySpreadConstraints.

**Pre-commit Hook:**
Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
```yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: topology-gate
        name: Enforce topologySpreadConstraints
        entry: python gate-topology.py
        language: system
        types: [yaml]
```
